On the payment side there are 3 open invoices with Adlerhof Trade Credit (CL01), total open exposure of EUR 189,100, with the worst item 25 days past due. The payment file is labelled "improving" because days-late fell from 46 and 55 days on the two oldest settled invoices to 10 days on the most recent, but that read rests on only three settled invoices and is contradicted by the one live position: INV001567, EUR 86,900, already 25 days past due.

The score is 47.7, placing the buyer in the Watch band with a PD of 0.3767. It is built as 0.65 x 33.3 (payment, 25 DPD) + 0.35 x 74.3 (news) = 47.7, so the payment leg contributes 21.7 and the news leg 26.0. The adjudicator agreed with caveats: the band is supported, but the two inputs are not independent — delayed wages and a past-due payment describe the same cash-flow strain — so 47.7 likely sits at the conservative end of what the evidence implies. The material weakness is concentration: 26.0 of the 47.7 rests on a single two-sentence article from one publication with no corroborating source, and that news component decays with age (base 75.0 already decayed to 74.29 at 5 days).

One insurer covers this buyer. For Adlerhof Trade Credit (CL01), limit LIM0040 is recommended to REDUCE from EUR 430,000 to EUR 285,373, cutting to the limit where expected loss meets the 25% appetite (pd 0.3767 against a pd_target of 0.25). Maximum liability does not bind, and expected loss falls from EUR 131,205 to EUR 87,075. The reduced limit still sits above the EUR 189,100 currently owed. Separately, the line has not been reviewed since 2024-10-24, leaving undrawn headroom available to a buyer now showing both payroll distress and a past-due position; that stale review is not captured anywhere in the score and should be refreshed independently of the band.

Recovery requires evidence on both legs, and the news leg should not be allowed to fade on its own. Because the news component decays with age, the buyer will drift back toward the Healthy band automatically in the coming weeks even if the wage arrears are never cleared, so an active re-check of payroll status is recommended rather than treating silence as improvement. Confirmation that the Essen wage arrears have been cleared and that the union has stood down would retire the severity 5 signal on its merits. On payments, clearing INV001567 (EUR 86,900) and bringing the 25 DPD position current would relieve the payment leg, and additional settled invoices beyond the current three would give the "improving" trend the depth it presently lacks against 45-day terms. A refreshed limit review would close the stale-line gap regardless of where the score lands.
